results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 36 prose and list units match their aligned spec paragraphs p01-p36 in spec order: intro context (research date, secondary summaries, 2026 names) and roadmap; R-number rules, exclusion of briefs with R566 as the exception, entry fields and evidence-type table; the placement rule and the thirteen topic blocks in identifier order; the thirteen entry lists; the per-chapter list; the reference chain, the check-before-citing advice and the limits of the evidence. The three opening callouts carry the spec's roadmap (IN THIS SECTION) and thesis statement (KEY POINTS) placements and the journal's failure-pattern callout; they are not spec paragraphs and are left unmatched.

results.quote: Some company pages blocked automated access during the research, and a few facts are known only through **secondary summaries** (a trade-press article or a third-party digest of an engineering post); the entries say so where the citing chapter did. Ownership and brand names follow the sources as of 2026: Schibsted is now Vend, eBay Kleinanzeigen is now Kleinanzeigen, and the former eBay Classifieds Group is part of Adevinta.
results.finding: The outliner needed two summaries (research timing and access caveats / current company names). The spec's single controlling idea is that the register records sources as the October 2026 research found them, and the naming rule belongs under it, but the paragraph never states that frame: its first sentence is the hook ('This page lists the external sources the chapters cite') and the naming sentence arrives as a second topic. A sentence saying that entries record each source as the October 2026 research found it (date, directness and name) would make it one paragraph.
No other unit was marked two_ideas by the outliner.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: intro ¶1 to B2 (age and directness of evidence), ¶2 to the roadmap and B4 (briefs not listed); How to Read ¶1 to B1, ¶2 to B1/B4, ¶3 and the table to B2; the Topic Index and Sources by Chapter to B3; the thirteen entry lists to B2/B3; the conclusion to B2 (check year and type) and B4 (Veldmark and judgement unsourced). Entry-level defects are judged under evidence_is_explained.

results.draft_locus: How to Read This Register ¶3 and evidence-type table
results.finding: The table is framed by 'The table below lists the twelve evidence types: read an entry's type together with its year to see how far it can support a claim', and each row's 'How to read it' column says what that type can support; the reasoning item (a company engineering post more than about three years old is a record of its date) is stated. Counts sum to 587.

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶1; How to Read ¶1; Topic Index ¶1; Sources by Chapter ¶1
results.finding: Each fact or reasoning item is stated with what it shows: the October 2026 research and naming; deduplication and never-reused R-numbers 'so a reference to an identifier keeps meaning the same document'; a multi-topic source keeps one place with a Cited in line listing every chapter; the per-chapter list is introduced as grouping the same sources by citing page.

results.draft_locus: Company sources: Adevinta and Schibsted ¶1 (R31, R53, R37/R38)
results.quote: — Adevinta tech blog, 2022 (possibly superseded). ANN index over items active in the last 90 days and viewed in the last 15. *Company filing or announcement.*
results.finding: The spec requires each entry to carry an evidence type that tells the reader how far to trust it (B2). R31 is a tech-blog post typed as 'Company filing or announcement', which the table defines as 'authoritative on the company's reported numbers' — the opposite of how a 2022 engineering post should be read; it should be Company engineering (and the table count would change). In the same list R53 prints its access note twice ('undated (read October 2026). (read October 2026).') and R37 and R38 each give 'FINN help center, 2025 and 2024 (both updated 2026)', so neither single page has a readable year.

results.quote: **R351** · [Caches and query warming](https://solr.apache.org/guide/solr/latest/configuration-guide/caches-warming.html) — Apache Solr Reference Guide, n.d. — soft commits, commit intervals, caches cleared on new searchers.
results.finding: Each entry should give one clause on what that source supports. R351's clause is copied from R350 (Commits and transaction logs) and describes soft commits and commit intervals, which a caching page does not document, so the entry misstates what it supports. Other shared clauses the readers flagged (R352/R353, R360/R361, R507/R508, R543/R544, R568/R569, R37/R38) read as one joint claim the chapter cited two pages for and still fit both titles; they are not failed, but a 'cited together for' note would remove the appearance of a copy error.

results.quote: — DGFiP via data.gouv.fr, 2026 (last updated 12 October 2026). (updated twice a year) — the real French open dataset of property transactions on which the fictional Valuo is described as trained.
results.finding: The entry breaks the entry format (a stray parenthetical sentence and a dash after the date) and names 'the fictional Valuo', which appears nowhere else on the page. B4 asks the register to keep fiction distinct from documented fact; the page introduces only Veldmark as fictional, so a reader cannot tell what Valuo is or that it is part of the Veldmark story. Saying 'Veldmark's fictional valuation model, Valuo' (or dropping the name) would keep the entry to what the source supports.

results.spec_locus: remaining entry lists p20, p22-p26, p28, p30-p32
results.finding: Entries give identifier, linked title, publisher, year (or n.d. with read date), a clause on what the source supports, an evidence type and Cited in pages. R489 (NAR settlement FAQ typed Standard or specification) is arguable as an industry-body source, not a clear mistype; the separator inconsistency ('n.d. —' vs 'n.d.') is cosmetic.
'Those dates, summaries and names are part of every entry, so the page opens with…' picks up when and how sources were consulted and elaborates into the layout and the exclusion of briefs.

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶2 -> How to Read This Register ¶1
results.finding: The heading 'How to Read This Register' takes up the roadmap's first item ('how to read an entry') and the section opens on the identifier, the first field of an entry; the sequence is clear.

'Only public sources get an R-number, with one exception named below' elaborates what gets an identifier; 'Each entry gives the identifier, …' moves in sequence to the other fields and the evidence types.

'Identifiers run in topic order, so each topic is one contiguous block' picks up 'Identifiers were assigned in topic order' from How to Read ¶1; each block paragraph opens with its bold label and R-range, which continues the range ending before it (example for R1-R8, sequence thereafter).
Each topic section opens under its heading with the next R-number after the previous section, in the order the Topic Index announced; the declared sequence is expressed by heading and range.

results.draft_locus: Architecture method and organization -> Sources by Chapter ¶1
results.finding: 'The topic sections group the sources by subject; this list groups them by the page that cites them.' expresses the declared contrast.

results.draft_locus: Sources by Chapter -> From Template to Source ¶1 -> ¶2 -> ¶3
results.finding: 'A chapter's line above is the last link in one reference chain…' carries over the chapter line; 'So before you cite a source…' expresses cause-effect; 'The chain stops where the evidence stops.' turns from what the sources support to what none supports (contrast).

Both readers describe the declared organising principle: orientation (how to read, topic map) before the entries, the entries grouped into thirteen topic sections in identifier order (economics, company sections in case-chapter order, technical topics, method), then lookup by chapter and the close. This agrees with prerequisite_order plus grouping. Failed points follow.

results.quote: (Platform, data, ML and experimentation precedes Web, SEO and reliability, the reverse of their chapters, because the topic list the identifiers were assigned from put them in that order)
results.finding: flow-reader-A §3a: 'This is the worst spot. The reason given is just "it was in that order." "The topic list the identifiers were assigned from" has not been introduced anywhere. I re-read it twice.' Both readers call the reason circular, and the parenthesis sits inside a paragraph that packs four rules (A §3e). The spec's p06 prescribes exactly this explanation and its unintroduced referent; the honest reason (the order was fixed with the identifiers, which are never renumbered, so a reference keeps meaning the same source) is what the reader needs. The spec should replace the 'topic list' reason before the prose can.

results.quote: The research briefs mentioned in the opening are left out: the chapters rely on these briefs, written in October 2026 to collect and check the company, regulatory and practice facts the chapters use.
results.finding: flow-reader-A §3b: 'After the colon I expected the reason they are left out. Instead I got the reason they matter … I had to re-read.' The spec's order (exclusion, then reason, then the public source listed instead) is fine; the colon promises a reason the sentence does not give. Lead with 'Those briefs are working notes, not public evidence' and put what the chapters use them for after it.

results.draft_locus: Introduction callout (FAILURE PATTERNS THIS SECTION ADDRESSES)
results.quote: **The Forced Fit** — company engineering posts are the largest evidence type on this page, and each describes one group's platform at one date
results.finding: flow-reader-A §3c: the callout 'comes before the page has said anything about evidence types … It felt out of place on a bibliography.' The callout is not part of the spec's introduction; it interrupts the opening before the reader knows what the page is. Move it after How to Read This Register, or drop it from this reference page.

flow-reader-B §2 marks Architecture method and organization 'Stated, but not why. Unclear.' Flow-reader-A rates it clear. The spec's p06 gives no reason either, so the gap starts in the spec; a clause such as 'whose chapters close the book' would place it.

results.quote: A topic index then maps the thirteen topic sections that hold the entries, six of them on company groups or kinds of marketplace, and a list of the sources each chapter cites follows them.
results.finding: flow-reader-B §3: 'I re-read this. "Follows them" is ambiguous (follows the index, or the sections?), and the sentence packs three ideas into one.' Split the sentence: the topic index, then the thirteen sections, then the per-chapter list after them.

results.quote: The toolkit presents each template as the smallest form that makes a decision explicit, assigns an owner and leaves evidence someone else can check.
results.finding: flow-reader-B §3: 'A small digression in the middle of describing the reference chain; I re-read to connect it to the next sentence.' The callback is required, but placed between the chain and 'This chain is how that check is made' it reads as a new topic; tie it in a clause (e.g. 'The toolkit asks each template to leave evidence someone else can check; this chain is how…').

results.quote: EU, UK and US law, competition decisions, RFCs, schema.org, RESO, OpenImmo, address registries and advertising standards.
results.finding: RESO and OpenImmo are property-listing feed standards, which the spec lists as unknown to this audience, and the prose (not an entry) names them with no gloss. Definitions are a non-goal here, but a two-word gloss ('the RESO and OpenImmo property-listing standards') keeps the topic map readable without defining them.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-A §5 (RESO and OpenImmo); flow-reader-B §5 (Standards and formats: RESO, OpenImmo)

results.finding: The many unexplained terms the flow readers list (GMV, CUPED, percolation, DAC7, P2B, strangler fig, the 88-capability skeleton in R566, etc.) occur inside entry descriptions harvested from the chapters; the spec makes definitions a non-goal covered by the glossary, and How to Read ¶2 points there ('Plain-language definitions of the terms used in the entries are in [[glossary]]'). Veldmark, Productscape, Aurelia UK Feederco, Vend and 'secondary summaries' are glossed where first used. 'The Forced Fit' is glossed in its callout and links to its defining page; its placement is failed under flow_is_followable.

Direct-statement hook ('This page lists the external sources the chapters cite.') followed by concrete scope and caveats; not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary opening, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The intro reader predicted the four parts in order (how to read, topic index and thirteen sections, per-chapter list, close linking toolkit and glossary), the evidence types and the cautious tone, and gave every element of AC-2's expected answer: only cited sources, each once, with year, type and Cited in pages, findable by topic or chapter; October 2026 research, secondary summaries, 2026 names; research briefs and Veldmark not sources; weigh claims by kind and age. Its residual doubts (index vs sections, how secondary entries are marked) are minor and answered by the body.

Opens from the last section's chapter lines, does not begin 'in conclusion', adds no new evidence, and ends on the limits of the evidence rather than a restated thesis; none of the named weak patterns.

States what no section does — template field -> glossary row -> chapter line -> dated sources across the three reference pages — and why it matters: 'a decision record built from the book can be traced through its definitions to evidence of a known kind and age', followed by the course of action before citing.

Returns to the toolkit's 'leaves evidence someone else can check' ('This chain is how that check is made') and to the KEY POINTS distinction ('Veldmark is fictional; architectural recommendations and labeled inferences are the author's judgement').

results.draft_locus: Company sources: eBay Classifieds… (R134); Sources by Chapter; evidence-type table; How to Read ¶3
results.finding: The AC-1 reader found R134 both through the eBay Classifieds/Kleinanzeigen/Marktplaats topic section and through the citing chapters' lines in Sources by Chapter, and judged it from its type and year exactly as expected: a company engineering post 'documents what the company says it built at that date; it may describe systems since replaced', and at seven years old it is 'a record of that date, not of today'. Its doubts (which brand 'Berlin Tech Blog' belongs to; no pointer to newer sources) do not block the outcome.
